entry.name: stretch~
entry.digest: Ztx-based pitch/time modification of an audio buffer
entry.description: Use the stretch~ object to perform destructive pitch and time modifications to the contents of a buffer~. object.

arguments.name: buffer-name

attributes.name: mode
attributes.digest: Timestretching Mode
attributes.description: Sets the timestretching mode to be used. Each mode is optimized for handling different kinds of audio material

choices.label: This is the default mode of operation.
This mode is best for monophonic instruments (e.g. solo voice, flute, etc.)
This mode is for time stretched percussion. It provides optimal transient preservation.

choices.digest: Balance spectral integrity with transient preservaton
choices.label: This mode balances spectral integrity and transient preservation for general cases.
Polyphonic mode is a better choice for instruments such as piano or guitar.

choices.digest: Emphasize spectral quality over transient preservation
choices.label: This mode emphasizes spectral quality over transient preservation.
This mode is intended for stretch ratios greater 2.0, a more artistic effect is intended.
This mode is intended for a good CPU performance/quality tradeoff.

attributes.name: slurtime
attributes.digest: Slur time
attributes.description: Set the time it takes for the correction to reach the full correction amount. Typically, notes are a bit unstable at the beginning, because the attack phase of a sound has a higher amount of noise, and because singers gradually adjust their tuning after the onset of the note. The slur time makes the pitch correction sound natural because it models this effect. Higher values will yield a slower adaptation time and it will take longer for the correction to produce the corrected pitch. However, longer slur times will also preserve vibrato better.

attributes.name: stretch
attributes.digest: Stretch factor
attributes.description: Set the timestretching as a factor in relation to the length of the current buffer (e.g. 2.0 = double the length, .5 = half the length, etc.).
